newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan electronics sink despite chip price rebound.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan electronics sink despite chip price rebound.

text.p: Taiwan's recently hot electronic shares fell sharply at mid-session on Friday as profit-taking gripped the sector despite a global recovery in memory chip prices, brokers said.
With 65 minutes left electronics, which had led the market during the market's previous eight consecutive sessions of gains, had fallen by 1.50 percent.
Taiwan Semiconductor, the island's top chipmaker, lost T$2.50 or 3.94 percent to T$61 on heavy trade volume of 26.72 million shares.

Brokers said investors largely ignored recent news that prices for 16-megabit dynamic random access memory chips, which had tumbled in 1996, had rebounded to around US$10 per unit from $6-$8 a month ago.
"Taiwan's chip companies have already risen on that piece of news. It is nothing new to the market," said Chen Han-chung, analyst for Yungli Securities.
"Local factors like profit-taking are far more influential in the market today (Friday)," he added.
